blocks.text: Menahem gives Pul silver so that Assyrian support will confirm his rule (vv. 19-20). That makes this payment a calculated effort to secure his kingdom, but tribute should not automatically be treated as evidence for one fixed kind of relationship or a ruler's complete motives. Elsewhere in Kings, payments and refusals of tribute serve different political and literary functions.

Tiglath-pileser's capture of northern Israelite places and deportation of their inhabitants is a major loss in this chapter (v. 29), but it should not be compressed into every later stage of Israel's downfall. Kings presents territorial loss, Samaria's siege, deportation, and later resettlement through several notices; distinguishing those stages keeps this verse from being made to carry the whole later history at once.
